question.text: IRIS+ is offered by which body, and what is its core purpose in the impact-investing ecosystem?

answer.text: ICAI SIAB — to catalogue SAS-100 through SAS-1600 mandatory standards for SIAs
SEBI — to regulate Social Stock Exchange disclosures under ICDR 292A-L
Global Impact Investing Network (GIIN) — to provide generally accepted impact definitions, themes and core metrics aligned with SDGs
B Lab (B Corp) — to certify for-profit companies that meet social and environmental performance standards

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 6, IRIS+ is an impact accounting system offered by the Global Impact Investing Network (GIIN). It provides generally accepted definitions, impact categories, impact themes and core metrics aligned to SDGs, creating a shared language for impact measurement across investors. The Trap: ICAI SIAB publishes SAS standards in India; SEBI regulates SSE listing; B Lab runs the B Corp certification and B Impact Assessment — they all relate to impact but IRIS+ is GIIN's product. Cross-Exam Context: V-B Mutual Fund Foundation mentions global indices; XIX AIF references GIIN-style taxonomies for Cat I funds. For XXIII, IRIS+ sits alongside GIIRS, GRI and SASB as complementary tools, not substitutes. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When an overseas impact investor asks whether your Annual Impact Report metrics are IRIS+-aligned, map the SAS indicator IDs to the IRIS+ catalogue in an appendix — it dramatically shortens foreign-investor diligence cycles.
